reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space with its Borel σ-algebra, μ a measure on E, and C∈ℝ. Write h(t)=t log t for t>0 and h(0)=0, and define A(g)=∫_E h(g²) dμ−h(∫_E g² dμ) and D(g)=∫_E ‖∇g‖² dμ, with the real-valued integral interpreted as zero for nonintegrable integrands. Suppose A(v)≤2C D(v) for every smooth compactly supported v:E→ℝ. Then A(f)≤2C D(f) for every smooth f:E→ℝ such that f∈L²(μ), ∇f∈L²(μ;E), and h(f²) is μ-integrable.
objects: The measure μ, real constant C, compactly supported test function v, target function f, square-log function h, entropy expression A, and gradient energy D.
domains: E is a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with the Borel σ-algebra. Both v and f map E to ℝ; gradients are E-valued. All integrals are over E for the same μ.
quantifiers: For every admissible E, measure μ, and C∈ℝ, if the inequality holds for all smooth compactly supported v, then it holds for all smooth f satisfying the listed integrability conditions.
assumptions: The premise is the inequality A(v)≤2C D(v) for all smooth compactly supported v, with no separate integrability hypotheses on v. The target f is C∞, f and ∇f are square-integrable, and h(f²) is integrable. No finiteness or probability normalization of μ is stated.
conclusion: For each such f, ∫_E h(f²) dμ−h(∫_E f² dμ)≤2C∫_E ‖∇f‖² dμ.
scopes: The universal test-function premise is evaluated at fixed E, μ, and C before quantifying over the target functions. Compact support is required only of v; the three integrability conditions are listed only for f. Smoothness means all finite derivative orders, not analyticity.
constant_dependencies: The same arbitrary real C appears in the premise and conclusion, always with the multiplier 2. There is no positivity hypothesis on C, no assertion that such a C exists, and no change of C with f.
